subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: After fixing authorization ordering, should plugin-runtime callers fail closed on every legacy ownerless session row, or should OpenClaw provide an explicit ownership migration path?
rationale: The original bug establishes that foreign-owned rows require isolation, but it does not define authority for persisted rows created before ownership metadata existed.

options.title: Fail closed on ownerless rows
options.body: Keep legacy ownerless rows operator-only and require plugins to create new rows carrying their authenticated ownership.

options.title: Add explicit ownership migration
options.body: Provide a separate auditable doctor or operator action that assigns ownership without permitting arbitrary runtime adoption.

recommendation.title: Fail closed on ownerless rows
recommendation.body: Keep legacy ownerless rows operator-only and require plugins to create new rows carrying their authenticated ownership.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent session-storage boundary work is the strongest available routing signal for this persisted authorization and migration decision.
